claim: Impact 1: "about 3–7 staff hours a year (12–24 inquiries x 15–20 minutes each x 100% captured)" = "about $86–$200 a year"
problem: Minor arithmetic slip: the stated inputs give 3–8 hours (24 x 20 min = 8 h) and therefore about $86–$230. The quoted 3–7 h / $86–$200 pair is internally consistent but drops the top of the input range, so the figure is understated rather than inflated. Nothing rests on it, and the surrounding text already calls the saving "smaller", so it does not mislead.
fix: Change to "about 3–8 staff hours a year ... = about $86–$230 a year", or keep 3–7 h and describe it as an already-discounted upper bound.

claim: "the domain is yours, the page is not" (opener) and "The domain is still registered to you and paid through December 2030" (founder email)
problem: Minor framing issue: the cited RDAP record shows registration 2010-12-07, expiry 2030-12-07, GoDaddy client locks and NJ nameservers, but the registrant is redacted, so who holds it is an inference from the brand domain and listings, not a stated fact. Stating it flatly to the owner is safe in practice (he can confirm it in seconds) but it is not traceable to the source as written. Same for "paid": the record shows an expiry date, not a payment.
fix: Soften to "the domain is still registered and locked at GoDaddy with an expiry in December 2030 — the registrant isn't public, but it looks like yours and recoverable" and drop "paid through" to "expires December 2030".

claim: Prep note: "our BLS extracts did not record the reference year, so the rates above are stated as approximate"
problem: Minor and internal-only: the BLS API series now returned clearly do carry the year (2025, annual, period A01 = May 2025 OEWS) for both OEUS340000000000043405113 (47,740) and OEUS340000000000047101113 (105,510). The hedge is unnecessary and slightly inaccurate about the source.
fix: Replace with "Rates are May 2025 OEWS annual medians for New Jersey, from the BLS Public Data API; the x1.25 benefits load is our assumption."

claim: Section 3 impact "about 62–145 staff hours ... = about $3,931–$9,194 a year"
problem: Not an error, but the audit's Section 3 range is narrower than analysis.json's $3k–$12k: the analyst's figure also counted 1–2 goodwill callbacks a month at the NJ roofer median, which the audit drops and replaces with a 60–70% automated-share assumption. Arithmetic checks out (52 x 2 x 60% = 62; 52 x 4 x 70% = 146; x $63.41 = $3,931 / $9,194), so a reader comparing the two documents will see different numbers for the same opportunity.
fix: Add a half-clause, e.g. "this counts record-keeping time only; callback labor is excluded", so the difference from the internal model is explicit.

claim: "It fits what you already run: GoDaddy domain, WordPress, Google profile, Birdeye and ProvenExpert listings, current number."
problem: Minor tense issue: WordPress describes the pre-compromise stack (verified in the 2025-05-18 and 2026-04-20 archive captures). The live install today is the spam page, so "what you already run" slightly overstates the present state — though GoDaddy, the listings and the number are all current and correct.
fix: Write "your old WordPress site, the GoDaddy domain, the Google, Birdeye and ProvenExpert listings and your current number are all reusable".
